headline: Nasdaq-100: an unresolved hawkish repricing meets the last closed hour before the futures reopen
body:
This assessment falls in the final hour of the weekend CME halt. The September contract is still marked closed on the exchange at 29,491.75, down 0.69% on Friday's session with a 29,436.25-29,811.50 range from a 29,635.50 open and 572,070 contracts of volume, so no live NQ price path exists and no mean-reversion failure can be developing. The cash anchor, re-verified this hour from the index history, is Friday's completed session: NDX opened 29,545.90, reached 29,752.78, fell to 29,383.92 and closed 29,433.43, down 0.70% from a 29,641.56 previous close, leaving the close about 50 points off the low of a 369-point range. VIX closed 14.43 within a 14.13-14.84 range, carrying no volatility premium into the weekend.

The macro driver remains a hawkish repricing rather than a price-path event, and it is still unresolved. The Federal Reserve's published Jackson Hole keynote by Chairman Kevin Warsh states that "inflation is running above our 2 percent target" and that policymakers "must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed. Otherwise, we have work to do." The reaction concentrated at the front end: the 2-year yield jumped more than 12 basis points to about 4.356% intraday, the 10-year rose more than 5 basis points to about 4.726% and the 30-year 2 basis points to about 5.211%. The H.15 release carries official constant-maturity yields only through 27 August at 4.20% for the 2-year, 4.38% for the 5-year, 4.67% for the 10-year and 5.19% for the 30-year, so the repricing is a Friday market move the official series has not yet absorbed. Verified weekend reporting frames the September outcome as a coin toss: implied odds moved from about 35% to a range of roughly 46% to 60% depending on the venue, one large-bank chief economist describes it as a close call while still expecting a hold, and bond investors at several managers are reported as sceptical of the hike wagers. That is a two-way debate whose resolution depends on the coming week's employment and inflation data, not a settled directional catalyst.

Cross-asset evidence conflicts rather than aligns. The latest session left the semiconductor complex uniformly lower, none of the seven tracked names positive, with NVDA down 4.57%, ARM down 6.33%, INTC down 2.85% and AMD down 2.33%, while the megacap tape was split five to three higher, led by AMZN up 3.97% with AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL and META all higher. Technology fell 1.41% while Communication Services rose 1.44% and Consumer Cyclical 1.36%. That is rotation, not a uniform risk-off impulse. Gold fell 2.88% and Treasury futures were lower across ZT, ZF, ZN and ZB, consistent with the hawkish repricing, while WTI was little changed on the day and finished last week about 4% lower. Under the risk definitions in force, conflicting internals reduce directional conviction and raise Stress; they are not an amplifier of the pathological price path Tail measures. Verified reporting continues to describe the Iran situation as a sanctions and economic confrontation rather than an imminent threat to physical supply, and no fresh geopolitical discontinuity is verified as of this cutoff.

None of the amplifiers that would justify a higher Tail are present: there is no observed persistent directional efficiency, no shallow-pullback sequence, no repeated extension after failed retracements, and no open market in which any of those could be forming. Tail therefore rests at the low-band floor of 5 and the mapped policy state is EA_ON. Stress at 32 reflects the untested front-end repricing meeting a data-heavy week: ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on Tuesday, ADP and the Broadcom report on Wednesday, ISM Services on Thursday and August payrolls on Friday, where published estimates cluster near 65,000 to 80,000 jobs after July contracted by 23,000. One narrow observation window is flagged across the 22:00-23:30 UTC Sunday reopen, now roughly half an hour away, where that repricing first meets thin liquidity and two-way gap risk. Monday 31 August is also month-end, and the UK summer bank holiday leaves London closed, thinning European depth through the day. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, covering the weekend halt from Sunday evening one day back through the hour before this one. The series was uniformly green with Tail fixed at 5, dominant mode normal, and Stress confined to a 25-31 band that drifted up only across the final hours as the reopen approached. Confidence decayed from 64 to 58 through the overnight hours as published evidence aged across the closed market, then recovered through 64, 72 and 80 to 86 as primary sources were re-verified on each hourly refresh. No hour in the window contained an observable NQ price path.
outlookSummary: The current hour is the last inside the weekend CME halt, where no price path can form; Tail stays at the low-band floor of 5 with Stress at 32 and Confidence at 87. From the projected 22:00 UTC reopen the conditional Tail lifts to 12, still inside the low band and far below the block threshold, covering the first live test of Friday's front-end repricing. It then eases through 11 and 10 across the Asian session to an overnight trough of 8, lifts through 9 and 10 into a continental-only European morning thinned by the UK bank holiday, and reaches a projected peak of 15 across the 13:00-14:00 UTC hour containing the U.S. cash open, where opening-auction imbalance meets month-end rebalancing on the final session of August. It eases through the U.S. afternoon before a secondary lift to 13 in the month-end closing hour, then settles at 10 after the close. Every projected hour maps to EA_ON and green; Stress peaks at 36 in the moderate band and Confidence decays to 69 at the far end of the projection.
